record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is there a morphism over 5 letters with two eigenvalues of norm smaller than 1 and an abelian-square-free fixed point?

evidence.quote: Is there a morphism over 5 letters with two eigenvalues of norm smaller than 1 and an abelian-square-free fixed point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be an alphabet of 5 letters and let $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ be a morphism. The incidence (or frequency) matrix of $h$ is the $5\times 5$ integer matrix $M_h$ whose $(a,b)$-entry equals the number of occurrences of the letter $a$ in $h(b)$. A right-infinite word $\mathbf{w}\in\Sigma^\omega$ is called a fixed point of $h$ if there exists a letter $a\in\Sigma$ with $h(a)=au$ for some $u\in\Sigma^+$ and $\mathbf{w}=\lim_{n\to\infty}h^n(a)$. Two finite words $u,v\in\Sigma^*$ are called abelian equivalent if, for every letter $c\in\Sigma$, the number of occurrences of $c$ in $u$ equals the number of occurrences of $c$ in $v$. A finite word is an abelian square if it can be written as $uv$ with $u,v$ abelian equivalent and $|u|=|v|\ge 1$. A word $\mathbf{w}$ (finite or infinite) is abelian-square-free if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is an abelian square.

Question: Does there exist a morphism $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ over a 5-letter alphabet $\Sigma$ such that the incidence matrix $M_h$ has at least two eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of complex modulus strictly less than $1$, and such that $h$ admits an abelian-square-free infinite fixed point?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces a thesis on avoidability of abelian repetitions discussing 5-letter abelian-square-free morphisms and eigenvalues of their incidence matrices, but no source confirms a definitive resolution (positive or negative) of this specific question. The status thus appears unresolved in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of Abelian Repetitions in Words (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses abelian-square-free morphisms over 5 letters and eigenvalues of their incidence matrices, including a morphism with an eigenvalue of modulus < 1.
status_evidence.claim: Related work exists on 5-letter abelian-square-free morphisms and eigenvalue conditions, but the specific existence question with two eigenvalues of modulus < 1 is not reported as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Fixed points avoiding Abelian k-powers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies decidability of avoidance of abelian k-powers in fixed points of morphisms under invertibility/eigenvalue assumptions on the frequency matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Related decidability results condition on eigenvalue properties of the incidence matrix, but do not settle the existence question stated.
